Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 94, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾

Tafsir (exegesis) of Surah Alam Nashrah

It is Meccan.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ mean: Did We not open up for you your breast? It has also been said: Did We not widen for you your breast? The first opinion was stated by Mujahid and al-Hasan.

Al-Suddi said: Did We not soften for you your heart? Al-Hasan, in another narration, said: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ means that it was filled with wisdom (hikmah) and faith (iman).

It has been reported in the traditions, through the narration of Qatadah, from Anas, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, that the Prophet of Allah said: "While I was near the House, between sleeping and waking, I heard someone saying: 'He is among the three.' Then I was brought a basin of gold containing Zamzam water, and Allah opened my breast up to such and such."

Qatadah said: I asked, "What do you mean?" He said: "To the bottom of my belly. Then my heart was extracted and washed with Zamzam water, then it was returned to its place, then it was filled with faith and wisdom."

In the hadith there is a long account. He said, may Allah be pleased with him: The judge and imam Abu al-Darda' informed us of this hadith; Abu al-Abbas ibn Siraj informed us; Abu al-Abbas ibn Mahbub informed us; Abu Isa al-Hafiz informed us; Muhammad ibn Bashshar informed us; Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Ibn Abi 'Adi informed us, from Sa'id ibn Abi ('Urubah), from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, the hadith.

It is a sound (sahih) hadith.

It has also been reported in the traditions that the Prophet said: "When the light enters the heart of the believer, it expands and spreads out."

It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there a sign of that?" He said: "Withdrawing from the abode of delusion, turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, and preparing for death before death arrives."

And His saying: ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾. Mujahid said: that is, We forgave you. This is in the sense of His saying, ﴿That Allah may forgive you your sins, past and future﴾.

And His saying: ﴿your burden﴾. Mujahid said: that is, your weight.

It is related from some of them: "And We removed from you your burden," that is, We lightened from you your weight.

And in a narration from Ibn Mas'ud: "And We unloaded from you your load."

And His words: ﴿Who had burdened your back﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, He made you bear a weight such that the sound of your back breaking could be heard from it. This is by way of comparison and illustration, meaning: if it were something heavy, the sound of your back breaking from its weight would be heard.

If someone says: What was that burden? And was he upon the religion of his people before prophethood or not?

The answer: It has been reported in the tafsir that he was upon the religion of his people before that. The meaning of this is that he would attend their gatherings and agree with them in some of their affairs, without worshipping an idol or venerating an idol-god. Allah had protected him from that. So what we have mentioned is the burden that had broken his back.

And His saying: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾. Regarding it there are several opinions. The first: "And We raised high your remembrance through prophethood and messengerhood."

The second: "We raised high your remembrance," meaning: "I made your obedience My obedience, and your disobedience My disobedience." The well-known view on this is: "I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned along with Me." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "In the adhan (call to prayer), the iqama (second call to prayer), the tashahhud (testimony recited in prayer), on the pulpits in the Friday congregation, in the sermons of the two ʿIds, on the Day of ʿArafa, and other occasions."

Qatada said: "There is no one reciting the tashahhud, no khatib (preacher), and no one leading a prayer, except that he calls out: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'"

This has also been transmitted in some reports as a statement traced back to Jibril, peace be upon him, through the narration of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said to me: "Indeed Jibril said: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'When you are mentioned, you are mentioned along with Me...'"

Hassan ibn Thabit said, praising the Prophet:

(Upon him is a radiant seal of prophethood, from God, witnessed, shining and bearing witness.)

(God joined the Prophet's name with His own name, when the muezzin proclaims in the five prayers, "I bear witness.")

(He derived from His own name a name for him, to honour him: "The Possessor of the Throne is Mahmud (the Praised), and this is Muhammad.")

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 94, verses 5–6:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾, meaning: with hardship comes ease.

In the exegesis it is related that the polytheists reproached the Prophet and his companions and said: "If you wished, we would gather for you some wealth so that you would return from this speech." This distressed him, so God the Exalted revealed this verse.

The meaning is: with poverty comes wealth, with constriction comes expansiveness, with difficulty comes ease, and with hardship comes comfort.

God has indeed fulfilled this in this world through what He opened to the Prophet – peace and blessings of God be upon him – and to his companions. God the Exalted opened to the Prophet the Hijaz, Tihama, what lies around them, most of the land of Yemen, and many of the deserts up to [near] Iraq and Syria. He opened to his companions what He opened, and they gained the treasures of Kisra and Caesar. The state of the Prophet at the end of his life became such that he would gift two hundred camels, or thousands of sheep, and would store up a year's provision for his household. This which we have mentioned is the meaning of the verse.

Ma'mar related, from Ayyub, from al-Hasan, that the Prophet went out one day, joyful, to his companions and said: "Rejoice, for no two hardships will ever overcome one hardship," and then he recited the saying of God the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾. He, may God be pleased with him, said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us of this hadith; Sahl ibn 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Barraz informed us; al-'Adhafari informed us; al-Dabari informed us, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar… the hadith.

If someone says: What is the meaning of his saying, "no two hardships will ever overcome one hardship," when both (words) have been repeated?

The answer to this: al-Farra' mentioned that when an indefinite noun is repeated as an indefinite noun, the second is other than the first; and when an indefinite noun is repeated as a definite noun, the second is the same as the first. The Arabs say: "I earned a dirham today, and I spent the dirham."

So the second is the first.

We say: On this meaning comes the saying of God the Exalted: ﴿As We sent to Pharaoh a messenger, but Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger﴾. And it is related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "If hardship were to enter a lizard's hole, ease would follow it until it extracted it."

Regarding the meaning of "two ease(s)" there are two opinions: one, the ease of this world; the other, the ease of the Hereafter. Accordingly, the meaning of the report is: if hardship overcomes the ease of this world, it does not overcome the ease of the Hereafter.

The second opinion: the first ease is for the Messenger, and the second ease is for his companions.

He, may God be pleased with him, said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Junjurdi informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Naysaburi informed us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Amir al-Baghdadi say: I heard 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya say: I heard 'Umar say: al-'Utbi used to say: I was one night in the desert, when a line of poetry came to my mind, so I said:

(I see death for one who wakes up... distressed, and departs.)

When the night grew dark, I heard a caller calling out from the air:

(Oh you, the person whose worry... will depart from him,)

(And he recited a verse... that has remained in his thought, flashing.)

(When your hardships have grown intense... then reflect on "Did We not expand?")

(Hardship between two eases... when you see it, rejoice.)

He said: So I memorized the verses, and God relieved my distress.

He, may God be pleased with him, said: Abu Bakr recited to us, saying: Abu Ishaq recited to us, saying: al-Hasan recited to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan recited to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Hiri recited to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bahlul the judge recited to us:

(Do not despair, even if you are in hardship one day, for you will have ease over a long time.)

(And do not think ill of your Lord, for God is more worthy of goodness.)

(Indeed, hardship is followed by ease, and the word of God is truer than every saying.)

He, may God be pleased with him, said: Abu Bakr recited to us, saying: Abu Ishaq recited to us, saying: al-Hasan recited to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad recited to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Mu'adh (al-Karkhi) recited to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari recited to us:

(When hardship reaches its utmost, then at that moment trust in swift ease.)

(Have you not seen the ill luck of the obstinate winter, followed by the wondrous good fortune of spring?)

He, may God be pleased with him, said: Abu Bakr recited to us, Abu Ishaq recited to us, 'Isa ibn Zayd al-Tufayli recited to me, Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Raqqi recited to me:

(Expect, when calamities have overtaken you, joy that will string them off from you, one by one.)

(You see God does not break His promise, and He has said: indeed, with hardship comes ease.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 94, verse 7:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So when you are free, then strive hard﴾. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: When you have finished the prayer, then exert yourself in supplication, and turn eagerly to God in your request.

Al-Sha'bi said: When you have finished the tashahhud, then supplicate for your worldly life and your next life.

Similar to this was narrated from al-Zuhri and from Ibn Mas'ud: When you have finished the obligatory duties, then exert yourself in the night prayer (qiyam al-layl).

And from some of them: When you have finished conveying the message, then exert yourself in jihad against the disbelievers.

And His saying: ﴿And to your Lord direct your longing﴾ is an exhortation to supplication (du'a') and asking (al-mas'alah).

Al-Zajjaj said: "To your Lord direct your longing alone, and let your longing not be directed to anyone other than Him."

And Allah knows best.
